newsitem.title: CHINA: China winter grain acreage seen up 2.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: China winter grain acreage seen up 2.2 pct.

text.p: China will increase acreage of wheat and other grains sown this autumn and winter by about 2.2 percent compared with a year ago, the China Daily said on Tuesday.
It did not give a figure for actual acreage but it quoted the State Statistical Bureau as saying the estimate was based on a survey of 40,000 farm households.
Wheat acreage alone would rise by 1.6 percent, the official newspaper said, adding that higher state purchase prices had convinced farmers to grow more grains this year.
Total winter crop acreage would rise by about 3.0 percent over last year, it said.
The survey found that all areas, except for northern Hebei and Shanxi provinces and the agricultural areas in Shanghai, would increase acreage for autumn and winter crops.

Acreage for oil-bearing crops this autumn and winter would rise by 0.6 percent over last year despite overproduction and low prices. Acreage sown and output had declined earlier in the year, the newspaper said.
Autumn and winter sowing had been completed in north China but was continuing in southern parts of the country, it said.
